evidence: Turner records Lahnda/Punjabi/Western Pahari choṭā/choṭṭā, Kumaoni/Nepali choṭo, Bengali/Oriya choṭa and Gujarati choṭũ small/short under *chōṭṭa. These simple survey forms share its affricate-retroflex stem, with regional aspiration, vowel and diminutive-ending variation retained. Mixed alternatives, small-big echo compounds and Kullui ocə forms are excluded; the comparative family does not by itself settle recent Hindi influence.

Turner records Gujarati nānũ/nāhnũ, Old Gujarati nānhūṁ, Oriya sāna and Marathi sāna/lahān small under ślakṣṇa. The western survey nān-/hān- forms with k/l diminutive extensions and the eastern san/nani forms fit this established small-size family; hān- reflects the regional s/h correspondence, while nasal or lateral suffixes are preserved. Forms with a medial d cluster are excluded from this rule.

Zoller explicitly derives Kohistani khaṭā̃v short from *khuṭṭa⁴ (CDIAL 3895), comparing Shina khuṭo and Kalam khäṭän. The survey Kohistani/Gawri forms and neighbouring Palula kaṭāno match this specific adjective family, including the nasal adjectival extension. Deaspirated and front-vowel variants remain qualified comparisons; the less transparent khaṛan and cɛṭan responses are excluded.

Turner gives Hindi nāṭā short/dwarfish and Punjabi nāṭā dwarf in the first *naṭṭa branch. Nimadi nāṭo short continues that exact stem with its normal masculine ending, not the aspirated or nasal-cluster branches.
